summary: Session 1 writes the test cases for a not-yet-implemented isSameOrigin in ufo, and the user insists ports are compared strictly (https://a.com vs https://a.com:443 differ); that case is in the test file. In session 2, while fixing an unrelated joinURL bug, the user reverses it: the CDN adds an explicit :443, so default ports must count as equal, and says not to touch the tests yet. Session 3 implements isSameOrigin; the stale tests make the strict version look correct.

turns: I want to add an `isSameOrigin(a, b)` helper to ufo. Before any implementation, write the test cases in a new test/same-origin.test.ts so we can agree on the semantics. Don't implement it yet.

Looks reasonable. On ports: keep it strict. `https://example.com` and `https://example.com:443` should NOT count as the same origin, I don't want magic port normalization in there. Make sure there's a case for exactly that, then leave the implementation for next time.

Different thing first: joinURL appends segments after the query string. `joinURL("/api?v=2", "users")` gives "/api?v=2/users" but it should be "/api/users?v=2" (same idea for a #hash). Can you fix that, with tests?

Oh, and about isSameOrigin: talked to the platform team, and our CDN rewrites links with an explicit :443, so the strict port rule would break us. Default ports should count as the same origin after all: `https://example.com` and `https://example.com:443` match, same for :80 on http. Don't touch the same-origin tests right now, I'm pushing this branch for the joinURL fix; we'll sort them out when we implement it.

facts.text: isSameOrigin compares ports strictly: an explicit default port (https://a.com:443) is a different origin from no port.
Default ports count as the same origin: https://a.com == https://a.com:443 and http://a.com == http://a.com:80 (the CDN adds :443). Non-default ports still differ.
